newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures drifted lower in a lacklustre session in which declines in U.S. bond prices undermined the positive impact of the eleventh cut in the French intervention rate this year.

The March bond future received a shortlived boost after the Bank of France shaved a modest five basis points off its key lending rate, which sets the floor for money market rates, but failed to hold onto its gains for long.
The short end of the curve benefited from the move which analysts said reinforced hopes that France would eventually bring interest rates down to the same level as those in Germany.

The spread between two-year bond yields in France and Germany narrowed to six basis points from 10 on Monday and French five-year yields ended 24 basis points lower than the equivalent German yields from 20 on Monday.
March 1997 interest rate futures climbed to set a new high at 96.71, implying that people expect three-month rates to be 3.29 percent at the end of March compared with 3.35 percent now.

"I think the objective is to close in on German rates but I do not think this is a victory for the thesis of ("dove" council members Paul) Marchelli and (Jean-Pierre) Gerard," Jean-Louis Mourier, economist, Louis Dreyfus Finance, said.

Traders and analysts said most expected the U.S. Federal Reserve to leave interest rates unchanged when its policy council meets on Tuesday. All 22 economists polled by Reuters last Friday said they expected the Fed to leave rates on hold.
The Treasury announced it would be selling 17 to 19 billion francs of two- and five-year BTANs at its regular monthly auction on Thursday.
The franc was slightly softer at 3.3767 against the mark compared with 3.3727 late on Monday.
